name: Grade 6 T2: mBot Movement, Debugging, and Outputs
description: Movement commands, sequence, speed, time, turns, debugging, outputs, LEDs, buzzers, and robot signals.

words.definition: An action that changes where or how a robot moves.
words.example: The program used movement commands to follow a path.

words.definition: Moving ahead in the direction the robot is facing.
words.example: The mBot moved forward for two seconds.

words.definition: Moving in the opposite direction from where the robot is facing.
words.example: The robot moved backward after hitting the wall.

words.definition: To change direction left or right.
words.example: The route needed one right turn.

words.definition: To end movement or pause an action.
words.example: The robot stopped at the finish line.

words.definition: The order in which commands happen.
words.example: The movement sequence was forward, turn, forward, stop.

words.definition: An instruction that tells the robot to do one action.
words.example: The command changed the robot speed.

words.definition: How fast something moves.
words.example: Changing the speed made the mBot travel farther in the same time.

words.definition: How long an action lasts.
words.example: The mBot moved for one second before stopping.

words.definition: To say what you think will happen before testing.
words.example: The class predicted the route made by a command list.

words.definition: To try a program and check what happens.
words.example: The team tested the robot after changing the turn time.

words.definition: To find and fix a mistake in a program or robot behavior.
words.example: The students debugged the program when the robot turned too far.

words.definition: To make something better after testing or feedback.
words.example: The group improved the route by changing the stop time.

words.definition: The path that a robot follows.
words.example: The route had three moves and two turns.

words.definition: The line or way a robot travels.
words.example: Floor tape marked the path for the challenge.

words.definition: An object or sign used to show a position or path.
words.example: The floor marker showed where the mBot should stop.

words.definition: Something a robot or computer does or shows after processing information.
words.example: An LED color is an output.

words.definition: A sound, light, or action that sends a message.
words.example: The robot used a buzzer signal when it finished.

words.definition: A small programmable light used as an output.
words.example: The LED turned red before the robot stopped.

words.definition: A part that makes a sound output.
words.example: The buzzer helped people know when the robot reached the finish.

words.definition: The current condition or situation of something.
words.example: The robot's state was start, turn, stop, or finish.

words.definition: Correct or close to the intended result.
words.example: The robot needed an accurate turn to stay on the path.

words.definition: A short explanation of what happened, what worked, and what could improve.
words.example: The student wrote a reflection about the movement problem.

words.definition: To show how something works.
words.example: The team demonstrated a working movement sequence.
